pathway.title: Hni Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business is large, spread across dealer and distributor channels and light on customer concentration, which supports revenue durability but does not remove cyclicality. Last-twelve-months net sales were USD 5,301.3 million and the five largest customers were about 13% of net sales, yet demand follows corporate office spending, which hybrid working keeps below historic occupancy, and housing activity for the hearth business. The company says backlog orders are typically cancellable and fulfilled within a few months and gives no backlog amount, so revenue visibility is short and rests on channel mix and management comment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 16–18, 85; calculation B1

Leverage is elevated and its fall so far comes from the earnings window, not from debt repayment. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell from 6.19x at 2026-04-04 to 3.07x at 2026-10-03, but net debt itself is USD 160.3 million above year-end and the window replaces pre-acquisition quarters with Steelcase quarters; on EBITDA before acquisition costs, restructuring and the inventory step-up, an analyst judgement, the ratio is 2.13x. The year-end ratio of 4.65x is the less reliable because it set full acquisition debt against under four weeks of Steelcase. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B5; calculation B6; calculation B7; calculation B8; calculation B9

Free cash flow is positive but thin once dividends are paid, which is the main reason debt falls slowly. Last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 132.7 million after capital expenditure and capitalized software is 9.80% of total debt, and dividends of USD 93.2 million leave USD 39.5 million, or 2.92% of total debt, before any other use of cash. Operating cash flow is seasonal, with an outflow in the first quarter and USD 195.3 million in the third quarter alone, so a single quarter overstates or understates the run rate. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 29; calculation B14; calculation B15; calculation B16; calculation B17; calculation B18; calculation B65

Earnings quality is the weakest part of the profile. Reported EBITDA margin was 7.63% for the last twelve months against 12.44% in FY2024, after Steelcase purchase accounting, restructuring and USD 94.9 million of acquisition costs in the window, and second-quarter margin was lifted by tariff refunds worth 240 bp of gross margin, about USD 35.3 million by analyst estimate and 150 bp of operating margin after tariff costs, with the third-quarter size not stated. The third-quarter EBITDA margin of 13.00% against 13.09% a year earlier shows the gap closing, but it is the strongest quarter so far in 2026, after margins of 2.88% in the first quarter and 10.75% in the second, and may include refunds that will not recur. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-04_hni-20260704.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 30–34; calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B53; calculation B19; calculation B20; calculation B63; calculation B64; calculation B25

Liquidity and maturities are a real support, with a refinancing question that starts in 2028. Cash and undrawn revolver of USD 490.3 million compare with a seasonal low of USD 327.4 million at 2026-04-04, and scheduled principal through FY2028 is only USD 61.2 million, but the USD 450.0 million of 2029 public notes are 32.75% of principal and the credit facilities carry springing maturities whose terms were not supplied, so the effective wall may arrive earlier than 2029. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–17; calculation B12; calculation B13; calculation B30; calculation B31

Debt service is manageable but exposed to rates. Net interest expense for the last twelve months was USD 80.5 million, covered 5.03x by reported EBITDA, and about 66.37% of principal floats; after the USD 100 million swap, a rise of 100 bp would add roughly USD 8.1 million a year, an analyst estimate. The financial covenants protect only the revolver and term loan A, 28.27% of principal, and the covenant definitions were not supplied, so headroom is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 18, 21; calculation B10; calculation B11; calculation B26; calculation B27; calculation B29; calculation B33

Financial policy is the main lever and it has leaned toward shareholders since the acquisition, which keeps the governance view at Medium. The Board raised the dividend and added USD 200 million to the repurchase authorization while net debt had not fallen, yet the record after the 2023 Kimball International acquisition, when debt was repaid, and the share-funded part of the Steelcase price argue for discipline. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 37, 42–43; calculation B68; calculation B59; calculation B57

The primary downside path is a demand slowdown before synergies and debt reduction are delivered. An illustrative fall of 10% in last-twelve-months net sales would remove USD 218.9 million of gross profit at the 41.29% gross margin if costs did not respond, taking reported leverage to 6.70x, and still reach 4.21x if half the loss were offset by cost action, against covenant levels of 4.25x stepping to 3.50x on definitions that were not supplied. Management has levers, namely the dividend, repurchases, capital expenditure and restructuring, but each competes with the others for the same cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 35–37; calculation B34; calculation B35; calculation B36; calculation B37; calculation B39; calculation B41; calculation B48

runs.text: The first strength is scale with low concentration: last-twelve-months net sales of USD 5,301.3 million and five largest customers of about 13% of sales spread revenue across many dealers and projects, so no customer loss alone threatens debt service. The second is cash generation: free cash flow was USD 173.8 million in FY2024, USD 208.5 million in FY2025 and USD 132.7 million over the last twelve months, which covers interest and scheduled amortization. The third is the hearth segment, earning a 17.81% margin and 31.19% of segment operating income, which cushions the larger furniture segment while housing holds. The fourth is liquidity and maturities, with USD 490.3 million of cash and undrawn revolver and no more than USD 22.5 million of scheduled principal a year until 2029. The fifth is the cost and synergy programme, which management says is slightly ahead of expectations. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 30; calculation B12; calculation B14; calculation B66; calculation B21; calculation B22; calculation B32; calculation B1

The first weakness is leverage that has not fallen in absolute terms, with net debt of USD 1,244.2 million, USD 160.3 million above year-end, which leaves less cushion against the covenant ladder. The second is thin free cash flow after dividends, USD 39.5 million over the last twelve months, which slows repayment. The third is earnings quality: a 7.63% EBITDA margin, provisional purchase accounting, restructuring that recurs and refunds of unstated size. The fourth is cyclical, housing-linked demand with limited visibility, and the fifth is a 2029 note maturity of USD 450.0 million with springing maturities in the facilities, which brings a refinancing test forward. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B5; calculation B9; calculation B3; calculation B16; calculation B30

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Steelcase merger was agreed on 2025-08-03 and completed on 2025-12-10 for total fair value of USD 1,922.3 million, made up of cash of USD 864.5 million, shares valued at USD 1,012.5 million and replacement awards valued at USD 45.4 million. Holders received USD 7.20 in cash plus a fixed fraction of an HNI share per Steelcase share, or an election that was prorated back to that mix, and the Board was enlarged by two to twelve seats for two Steelcase directors. Purchase accounting is provisional, with the allocation expected to be final in the fourth quarter of 2026. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 90–93; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; calculation A9

The cash price was financed with new senior secured facilities of USD 865 million under a credit agreement dated 2025-09-05, which equals the revolver, term loan A and term loan B balances at year-end, and with Steelcase cash that left a net cash outlay of USD 390.3 million. A further USD 351 million of Steelcase 5.125% notes due 2029 were exchanged into new HNI senior secured notes, leaving USD 99 million as unsecured obligations of Steelcase. In June 2026 the term loan B was refinanced with a USD 499 million tranche due 2032, and in September 2026 a dealer acquisition added USD 39.2 million of debt at 2026-10-03. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 63, 92, 102–106; 10-Q_2026-07-04_hni-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 14, 15–18; calculation A12; calculation A13; calculation A27

The filings do not give a sources and uses table, the terms of the indenture or the Amendment No. 3 margin, so the split of the facilities between price, repayment of existing debt and fees is not established, and the lien and guarantee terms of the secured notes are not known. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 92, 102–106; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five supplied filings are sufficient for a credit snapshot of Hni Corp through the quarter ended 2026-10-03, but only on the post-Steelcase perimeter, and covenant headroom cannot be tested because the credit agreement and its definitions were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings print the statements, the debt note with covenant levels, the segment note and the liquidity discussion, so Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit can run on them. Steelcase, acquired on 2025-12-10, is in the Q3 2026 figures but not in the prior-year columns, so the 133% rise in Q3 net sales reflects the acquisition and cannot be read as organic growth, and its purchase accounting is still provisional. No ratings, market prices, peer set, management adjusted-EBITDA bridge or filing after 2026-11-03 was supplied, which leaves the latest filing 15 days before the as-of date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Hni Corp (HNI Corporation, issuer hni-48287), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. It extracts the income statement, cash flow statement, balance sheet, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage figures from the five supplied filings, in USD millions, and states what the evidence supports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt is 3.07x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-10-03, down from 6.19x at 2026-04-04, but the measure blends full acquisition debt with about ten months of Steelcase earnings and a depressed fourth quarter of 2025, so it overstates run-rate leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5; 10-Q_2026-04-04_hni-20260404.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation C65; calculation C61

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt is USD 1,354.5 million, cash USD 110.3 million and the undrawn revolver USD 380.0 million. The year-end figure of 4.65x net debt to EBITDA is the less reliable, because it sets year-end acquisition debt against under four weeks of Steelcase and USD 94.6 million of acquisition costs. Cash interest is stated only for annual periods, so interest cover is calculable only for FY2024 and FY2025, and no issuer-adjusted EBITDA is stated, so no covenant ratio can be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14, 16; 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 73–76, 97; calculation C22; calculation C27; calculation C58; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt rose from USD 324.4 million at FY2024 to USD 1,083.9 million at FY2025 as the Steelcase financing replaced a much smaller debt stack, peaked at USD 1,373.7 million at 2026-04-04 on the first-quarter working-capital outflow, and fell to USD 1,244.2 million at 2026-10-03 as operating cash flow recovered after the first quarter. Net leverage on reported last-twelve-months EBITDA therefore fell from 6.19x to 4.42x to 3.07x across the three 2026 quarter ends, but most of the fall is the trailing window swapping pre-acquisition quarters for Steelcase quarters: net debt fell by only USD 129.5 million while EBITDA for the window rose from USD 222.0 million to USD 404.7 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-04-04_hni-20260404.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-07-04_hni-20260704.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; calculation C50; calculation C39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence to reading 3.07x as high is that the window still holds the fourth quarter of 2025, when reported EBITDA was only USD 0.5 million after USD 86.3 million of acquisition costs and with under four weeks of Steelcase. Before acquisition costs, restructuring and the inventory step-up, an Analyst Judgement and not an issuer figure, net leverage would be 2.13x. What would make the higher reading right is recurrence: restructuring and impairment charges were USD 43.1 million in nine months 2026, so some add-backs may repeat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 73, 75–76; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; calculation C46; calculation C47; calculation C49; calculation C77

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover on cash interest paid is 10.95x for FY2024 and 9.21x for FY2025, but both predate most of the acquisition debt: FY2025 cash interest was USD 25.3 million against net interest expense of USD 35.6 million, and net interest expense was USD 63.8 million in nine months 2026 alone. The quarterly reports do not state cash interest paid, so 2026 cover is not calculable on the method's definition; on net interest expense, last-twelve-months EBITDA covers interest 5.03x at 2026-10-03 and 4.37x at 2026-04-04.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 73, 76, 97; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C59; calculation C74; calculation C70

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow is strongly seasonal: USD -171.8 million in the first quarter of 2026, USD -32.0 million for six months and USD 163.3 million for nine months, so the third quarter alone produced USD 195.3 million. Last-twelve-months operating cash flow is USD 240.7 million and free cash flow after capital expenditure and capitalized software is USD 132.7 million, against nine-month dividends of USD 77.6 million and a USD 56.0 million repayment of loans against company-owned life insurance.

fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-10-03 was cash of USD 110.3 million plus USD 380.0 million undrawn on the USD 425.0 million revolver, USD 490.3 million in total, or 0.36x total debt. The revolver was drawn to USD 169.0 million at 2026-04-04, the highest of the quarter-end balances, which used about two-fifths of the commitment. Letters of credit and surety bonds of about USD 58 million are described, but the filing does not say whether any reduce revolver availability, so the undrawn figure may be overstated.

fields.value: Customer deposits, a non-interest-bearing contract liability, were USD 42.1 million at FY2024, USD 102.9 million at FY2025 and USD 117.6 million at 2026-10-03; USD 68.1 million of the FY2025 increase came with Steelcase. Supplier finance obligations were USD 31.2 million at FY2024, USD 26.1 million at FY2025 and USD 31.2 million at 2026-10-03. Both fund operations outside total debt and are not payables in the ordinary sense, so a fall in deposits or a withdrawal of supplier programmes would draw on cash or the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Lease obligations sit on their own balance sheet lines and are excluded from total debt: finance leases of USD 13.4 million and operating leases of USD 289.8 million at 2026-10-03. Company-owned life insurance policy loans of USD 99.8 million at FY2025 are netted against the asset rather than shown as debt, and USD 56.0 million was repaid in the third quarter of 2026; the balance after that repayment is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No issuer-stated EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA exists in the five filings, so reported EBITDA is built as operating income plus depreciation and amortization and excludes other non-operating income; the credit agreement's Consolidated EBITDA and Net Leverage Ratio are defined in documents that were not supplied, so every ratio here is a house measure and covenant headroom is not calculable. Printed dashes are treated as missing values, not zero, and four cash flow totals and one balance sheet total are left unstated because the filings' own rounding breaks the identity; each is listed under the gaps. Steelcase purchase accounting is provisional, so goodwill, intangibles, depreciation and amortization and therefore EBITDA comparisons can still move.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2025 annual report states a 53-week year with the extra week in the fourth quarter; FY2024 had 52 weeks. No subsequent event after 2026-10-03 is stated in the quarterly report signed 2026-11-03.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The segment net sales add to consolidated net sales and the segment operating income lines add to consolidated operating income in every column to within the filing's rounding. There are no intersegment sales of note: the filings call them immaterial.

fields.value: The instrument principal balances add to USD 1,373.9 million and, less USD 19.4 million of deferred issuance costs and discount, to total debt of USD 1,354.5 million at 2026-10-03.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No issuer-stated EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, Consolidated EBITDA or Net Leverage Ratio exists in the five filings and the Credit Agreement was not supplied, so reported EBITDA is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization and covenant headroom is not calculable for any period. Severity High. Obtaining the executed Credit Agreement and the quarterly compliance certificate would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is stated only in the annual supplemental note (USD 28.7 million for FY2024, USD 25.3 million for FY2025), so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable for 2026-04-04, 2026-07-04 and 2026-10-03; interim cover is shown on net interest expense as a labelled alternative. Severity High. The annual report for FY2026 would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The last-twelve-months window mixes perimeters: it holds the fourth quarter of 2025 (reported EBITDA of USD 0.5 million after USD 86.3 million of acquisition costs, and under four weeks of Steelcase) and between four and ten months of Steelcase depending on the date, while debt is the full acquisition financing. Pro forma net sales and net income are given by the issuer for FY2025, FY2024, Q3 2025 and nine months 2025, but no pro forma EBITDA or cash flow is supplied, so a like-for-like leverage ratio cannot be built. Severity High. A pro forma EBITDA from the issuer or a lender presentation would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Printed dashes are shown as not supplied rather than zero, as the method requires: acquisition and related costs for FY2024, Q1 2025, Q2 2025 and H1 2025; other non-operating income for FY2024 and the 2025 interim columns; asset impairment charges for FY2024 and 9M 2025; loss on sale of subsidiary for FY2024, H1 2026 and 9M 2026; net proceeds from sale of subsidiary for FY2024, H1 2026 and 9M 2026; acquisition spending for FY2024 and 9M 2025; the unconsolidated affiliate lines and other investing items for 9M 2025; purchases of common stock in Q1 and H1 2026; debt-issuance costs and COLI loan lines where only a dash is printed; inventory step-up for 9M 2025; and non-controlling interest for FY2025. Severity Low; the printed dash very probably means nil.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Some cash flow lines are not printed in every report: the annual report prints one combined working capital line while the quarterly reports print five detail lines, and the inventory step-up, COLI loan, unconsolidated affiliate, debt-issuance cost and property sale lines appear only in some reports. The non-controlling interest line is also not printed on the Q1 and Q2 2026 balance sheets. These cells are marked not supplied. Severity Low; totals are unaffected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Four cash flow totals and one balance sheet total are left not supplied because the filings' own rounding breaks an identity: Net Cash Change for FY2024 (printed -6.4, activity totals sum to -6.5), FY2025 (printed 195.4, sum 195.5) and H1 2026 (printed -105.3, sum -105.4); Net Cash Change for 9M 2026 (printed -98.7, but opening cash 217.9 plus -98.7 is 119.2 against printed closing cash 119.3); and Total Liabilities for FY2025 (printed 3,049.5, which with equity of 1,835.6 exceeds printed total assets of 4,885.0 by 0.1). Severity Low; each difference is 0.1.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity table by year is printed only at 2026-01-03, so the ladder does not reflect the June 2026 Term Loan B refinancing (a USD 499 million tranche due 2032), the Term Loan A and B amortisation since January, or the dealer debt assumed in September 2026 (USD 35.4 million at acquisition, USD 39.2 million outstanding at 2026-10-03). Severity Medium. The annual report for FY2026 would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Security and rank are not stated for the dealer's asset-based revolver (USD 27.2 million outstanding, USD 23 million described as assumed, commitment not stated) or its redemption note (USD 12.0 million due 2031, day not stated), and the lien priority of the HNI secured Public Notes against the Credit Agreement facilities is not stated. The dealer debt is left out of the debt stack and the notes are ranked on their stated label only. Severity Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The margin on the Term Loan B after Amendment No. 3 is not stated; the 2025 annual report gives 2.00% over term SOFR before the refinancing, and the quarterly rate fell from 5.8% at 2026-01-03 to 5.5% at 2026-10-03. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Whether letters of credit and surety bonds of about USD 58 million, and trade letters of credit of USD 6 million, are issued under the revolver or reduce its availability is not stated, so undrawn committed facilities may be overstated. Severity Medium. The revolver availability certificate would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Company-owned life insurance policy loans of USD 99.8 million at FY2025 are netted against the asset and are not in total debt; USD 56.0 million was repaid in the third quarter of 2026 and the remaining balance is not stated. Severity Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The dollar amount of tariff refunds recognised in cost of sales is not stated for Q3 2026 or nine months 2026; the second-quarter report gives only a margin effect, so the quality of 2026 gross margin cannot be sized. Severity Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No stand-alone Q4 2025 statement and no Q3 2025 balance sheet are printed; the fourth quarter is constructed as the fiscal year less nine months, and net debt at 2025-09-27 is not available. FY2023 and earlier periods in the annual reports, the Q1 and H1 2025 cash flow columns and the Q2 stand-alone cash flow were not extracted. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Steelcase purchase accounting is provisional and the quarterly report already lowered goodwill by USD 121.3 million and raised intangible assets by USD 281.0 million since the annual report; depreciation and amortization, and therefore reported EBITDA, can still change when the allocation is finalised in the fourth quarter of 2026. Severity Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No filing dated after 2026-11-03 was supplied, so events between 2026-11-04 and the as-of date of 2026-11-18 are not established, and the post-balance-sheet table records none found only for the sources read. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Hni Corp (HNI Corporation, issuer hni-48287), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. It sets out the Steelcase transaction and its financing, the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and financial-policy behaviour, and the dated events, from the five supplied filings. No sponsor is identified, so behaviour is read from the issuer's own actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors face a listed issuer with no identified sponsor or controlling holder, so Board discipline is the control, and it is untested: net debt of USD 1,244.2 million is above year-end while shareholder returns were widened, so risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 21, 37; 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 74; calculation A1; calculation A2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 1,083.9 million at year-end, and the nine months since brought free cash flow below dividends, USD 46.4 million of dealer investments and a USD 56.0 million repayment of loans against company-owned life insurance. Governance is otherwise conventional and transparent: the audit opinion is unqualified, acquisition accounting is updated each quarter, and the five filings document no priming, drop-down or related-party extraction. The gaps are provisional purchase accounting, a control review that excluded Steelcase, which is 63% of total assets, and credit documents that were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 25, 42; 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 69–73; calculation A2; calculation A3; calculation A24; calculation A36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor means no sponsor behaviour to score, and that is not an adverse finding. The filings describe one class of common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange with no preferred stock outstanding, no private-equity owner and no controlling holder identified. Former Steelcase shareholders were issued shares equal to 34.87% of the shares now outstanding, two of their directors joined a twelve-member Board and three named Steelcase shareholders signed voting support agreements for the merger, which points to larger holders among them, but the stakes are set out in a proxy statement that was not supplied and concentration is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Steelcase acquisition is a transformational, debt-funded step and the main governance risk. Total consideration was USD 1,922.3 million, of which cash was 44.97% and shares and replacement awards the remaining 55.03%, and USD 865 million of new secured facilities were drawn; total debt rose from USD 344.6 million at the end of FY2024 to USD 1,293.1 million at the end of FY2025, an increase to 3.75x the earlier level. Paying most of the price in shares limited the debt needed, but it also issued a new shareholder group a third of the equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 74, 90–93, 103–104; 10-K_2024-12-28_hni-20241228.htm.jsonl, page 64; calculation A4; calculation A7; calculation A8; calculation A9; calculation A10; calculation A11; calculation A12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy has not yet shown deleveraging: net debt rose USD 160.3 million from year-end to 2026-10-03. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 163.3 million less capital expenditure of USD 91.1 million left USD 72.2 million, which is below dividends paid of USD 77.6 million, and cash also went to USD 46.4 million of dealer investments, USD 24.1 million to acquire a dealer and a USD 56.0 million loan repayment. The company says earnings and cash are weighted to the second half, so nine months is a seasonally weak window, but the paydown that would reassure creditors is not yet visible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 29, 36; calculation A3; calculation A24; calculation A25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns were widened at the same time, a modest negative because they compete with debt reduction while the covenant tightens. On 2026-08-17 the Board declared a quarterly dividend of USD 0.35 per share, up 2.9%, and added USD 200 million to the repurchase authorization, which stood at USD 277.9 million at 2026-10-03 against USD 5.6 million actually spent in nine months. The company says it is committed to maintaining or modestly increasing the dividend, so the dividend is a hard-to-cut claim on cash, while the maximum net leverage ratio steps down from 4.25x to 4.00x and then to 3.50x within seven full quarters of closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 18, 21, 37, 43; calculation A33; calculation A34; calculation A35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The record after the 2023 Kimball International acquisition was creditor-aligned, which is the best evidence of how the Board treats acquisition debt. Total debt fell USD 91.2 million to USD 344.6 million during FY2024 as USD 100 million of the acquisition term loan was prepaid, even though dividends of USD 63.6 million and share purchases of USD 65.8 million continued. It was a smaller deal than Steelcase, so it supports intent rather than proving capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-28_hni-20241228.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 77–78; 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76, 106; calculation A4; calculation A5; calculation A6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is detailed, but the control picture is incomplete for the largest asset base. KPMG gave unqualified opinions and found internal control effective, yet management and the auditor excluded Steelcase, which is 63% of total assets and 7% of net sales, and the auditor named the preliminary valuation of acquired property and intangible assets as a critical audit matter. The allocation has already moved: goodwill fell USD 121.3 million and intangible assets rose USD 281.0 million, so assets and amortization can still change when the allocation is finalised in the fourth quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 69–73; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 42; calculation A30; calculation A31; calculation A36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor treatment so far is mixed rather than adverse, and legal capacity cannot be tested. The exchange offer moved USD 351 million of Steelcase notes into new HNI senior secured notes and left USD 99 million, 22.00% of the notes, as unsecured obligations of a subsidiary, so the two groups of holders now hold different claims; the June 2026 term loan B refinancing lowered the borrowing rate with other terms substantially unchanged. No uptier, drop-down, coercive exchange or collateral release appears in the five filings, but the credit agreement limits debt, liens, investments and restricted payments on customary terms whose baskets were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 37, 102–106; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18; calculation A28; calculation A29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earnings base is still being reset around one integrated furniture business. Workplace Furnishings is 88.99% of nine-month net sales and Steelcase alone is 55.55% of consolidated sales, while Residential Building Products earns 31.19% of segment operating income on 11.01% of sales. The Workplace Furnishings margin was 4.86% against 9.93% a year earlier after USD 110.9 million of Steelcase purchase accounting and USD 35.9 million of restructuring, and management calls synergies slightly ahead of expectations without stating an amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 25, 30; calculation A16; calculation A17; calculation A18; calculation A19; calculation A20; calculation A23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium level is that most of the Steelcase price was paid in shares, that the Board repaid acquisition debt after the Kimball acquisition, and that operations are improving: third-quarter net income was USD 90.0 million against USD 41.2 million a year earlier, and the company states it was in compliance with its financial covenants at 2026-10-03. If the second-half cash flow and synergy delivery hold, net debt should fall in the fourth quarter and the level would move toward Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move toward High if the Board funded repurchases or dividends with new borrowing while the covenant ladder tightens, if a waiver or amendment became necessary, if a single holder emerged with board control, or if the executed documents showed wide capacity to move assets or priority away from lenders. Receipt of the credit agreement, the indenture and the proxy statement would settle the legal-capacity and ownership questions in either direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement, which carries the beneficial ownership table, board independence and executive pay, was not supplied, so the finding that no sponsor or controlling holder exists rests on the annual report alone and would change if a large holder or special board rights were disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and the indenture were not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and new debt is not established; the Medium level rests on documented behaviour, and wide baskets would raise the risk of extraction without any change in conduct.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Steelcase purchase accounting is provisional and its controls were outside the management and audit assessments, so the integration-risk reading could change when the allocation is final in the fourth quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Synergy delivery is described in words only, with no amount or target in the filings, so the contrary case that integration is ahead of plan rests on management language and cannot move the level on its own.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No filing dated after 2026-11-03 was supplied, so shareholder-return or financing decisions taken since then are not established and could change the net debt trend that the Medium level relies on.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is Medium, driven by repeated debt-funded acquisitions, widened shareholder returns while net debt has not fallen, and a control and accounting position that is not yet final, because together they slow deleveraging and leave creditors dependent on Board choices that cannot be checked against the credit documents. Countervailing evidence is the share-funded 55.03% of the Steelcase price, the debt repaid after the Kimball acquisition, an unqualified audit opinion and the absence of any documented priming or extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 69–73, 90–93; 10-K_2024-12-28_hni-20241228.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 21, 37; calculation A3; calculation A11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Steelcase merger was agreed on 2025-08-03 and completed on 2025-12-10 for total fair value of USD 1,922.3 million, made up of cash of USD 864.5 million, shares valued at USD 1,012.5 million and replacement awards valued at USD 45.4 million. Holders received USD 7.20 in cash plus a fixed fraction of an HNI share per Steelcase share, or an election that was prorated back to that mix, and the Board was enlarged by two to twelve seats for two Steelcase directors. Purchase accounting is provisional, with the allocation expected to be final in the fourth quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cash price was financed with new senior secured facilities of USD 865 million under a credit agreement dated 2025-09-05, which equals the revolver, term loan A and term loan B balances at year-end, and with Steelcase cash that left a net cash outlay of USD 390.3 million. A further USD 351 million of Steelcase 5.125% notes due 2029 were exchanged into new HNI senior secured notes, leaving USD 99 million as unsecured obligations of Steelcase. In June 2026 the term loan B was refinanced with a USD 499 million tranche due 2032, and in September 2026 a dealer acquisition added USD 39.2 million of debt at 2026-10-03.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 63, 92, 102–106; 10-Q_2026-07-04_hni-20260704.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 14, 15–18; calculation A12; calculation A13; calculation A27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings do not give a sources and uses table, the terms of the indenture or the Amendment No. 3 margin, so the split of the facilities between price, repayment of existing debt and fees is not established, and the lien and guarantee terms of the secured notes are not known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every derived figure below is worked from the cited inputs in USD millions unless stated; ratios and shares are printed to two decimals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so board independence, committees, the independence and powers of the named Lead Director, beneficial ownership by holder and executive pay are not established, and the finding that no controlling holder exists rests on the annual report alone. Severity High. The 2026 proxy statement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement, the indenture and its supplements were not supplied, so baskets for restricted payments, debt, liens and investments, the guarantors and the collateral are not established and legal capacity cannot be separated from willingness. Severity High. The executed documents and compliance certificates would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sources and uses table is given for the Steelcase financing, so the split of the USD 865 million of facilities between the cash price, repayment of existing debt and fees is only partly established. Severity Medium. A closing funds flow would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No synergy target, timing or cost to achieve is stated, so the statement that synergies are slightly ahead of expectations cannot be sized. Severity Medium. The merger announcement presentation would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The obligor and any guarantee support for the USD 99 million of unexchanged notes are not identified, because the merger steps say Steelcase Inc. ceased to exist while the debt note calls the notes obligations of Steelcase as a subsidiary. Severity Medium. The Steelcase indenture would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Security, ranking and the commitment of the dealer asset-based revolver, and the day the redemption note falls due in 2031, are not stated. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Holdings, lock-ups and sales of the shares issued to former Steelcase holders, including three named holders who signed voting support agreements, are not stated. Severity Low. Beneficial ownership filings would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Sales to and balances with unconsolidated affiliates are stated only for 2025. Severity Low. The FY2026 annual report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No filing dated after 2026-11-03 was supplied, so events between 2026-11-04 and the as-of date of 2026-11-18 are not established. Severity Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Hni Corp (HNI Corporation, issuer hni-48287), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. It synthesises the business, financial and governance evidence in the five supplied filings and the earlier module handoffs into a credit view, ranked drivers, a downside path and monitoring triggers. It assigns no rating and makes no security recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hni Corp is an average-quality industrial credit in transition: a larger, cash-generative furniture and hearth business whose leverage is still elevated after Steelcase and whose free cash flow after dividends is thin, so creditors depend on delivered synergies to reduce debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B16; calculation B5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 1,244.2 million at 2026-10-03, or 3.07x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 404.7 million, backed by USD 490.3 million of cash and undrawn revolver and scheduled principal of no more than USD 22.5 million a year until 2029. Free cash flow of USD 132.7 million leaves only USD 39.5 million after dividends, and the maximum covenant ratio falls from 4.25x to 3.50x within seven full quarters of closing, so the next four quarters of margin recovery and debt paydown decide whether the view improves.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B5; calculation B2; calculation B12; calculation B32; calculation B14; calculation B16; calculation B48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is large, spread across dealer and distributor channels and light on customer concentration, which supports revenue durability but does not remove cyclicality. Last-twelve-months net sales were USD 5,301.3 million and the five largest customers were about 13% of net sales, yet demand follows corporate office spending, which hybrid working keeps below historic occupancy, and housing activity for the hearth business. The company says backlog orders are typically cancellable and fulfilled within a few months and gives no backlog amount, so revenue visibility is short and rests on channel mix and management comment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 16–18, 85; calculation B1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is elevated and its fall so far comes from the earnings window, not from debt repayment. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell from 6.19x at 2026-04-04 to 3.07x at 2026-10-03, but net debt itself is USD 160.3 million above year-end and the window replaces pre-acquisition quarters with Steelcase quarters; on EBITDA before acquisition costs, restructuring and the inventory step-up, an analyst judgement, the ratio is 2.13x. The year-end ratio of 4.65x is the less reliable because it set full acquisition debt against under four weeks of Steelcase.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B5; calculation B6; calculation B7; calculation B8; calculation B9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is positive but thin once dividends are paid, which is the main reason debt falls slowly. Last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 132.7 million after capital expenditure and capitalized software is 9.80% of total debt, and dividends of USD 93.2 million leave USD 39.5 million, or 2.92% of total debt, before any other use of cash. Operating cash flow is seasonal, with an outflow in the first quarter and USD 195.3 million in the third quarter alone, so a single quarter overstates or understates the run rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 29; calculation B14; calculation B15; calculation B16; calculation B17; calculation B18; calculation B65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is the weakest part of the profile. Reported EBITDA margin was 7.63% for the last twelve months against 12.44% in FY2024, after Steelcase purchase accounting, restructuring and USD 94.9 million of acquisition costs in the window, and second-quarter margin was lifted by tariff refunds worth 240 bp of gross margin, about USD 35.3 million by analyst estimate and 150 bp of operating margin after tariff costs, with the third-quarter size not stated. The third-quarter EBITDA margin of 13.00% against 13.09% a year earlier shows the gap closing, but it is the strongest quarter so far in 2026, after margins of 2.88% in the first quarter and 10.75% in the second, and may include refunds that will not recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-04_hni-20260704.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 30–34; calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B53; calculation B19; calculation B20; calculation B63; calculation B64; calculation B25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are a real support, with a refinancing question that starts in 2028. Cash and undrawn revolver of USD 490.3 million compare with a seasonal low of USD 327.4 million at 2026-04-04, and scheduled principal through FY2028 is only USD 61.2 million, but the USD 450.0 million of 2029 public notes are 32.75% of principal and the credit facilities carry springing maturities whose terms were not supplied, so the effective wall may arrive earlier than 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–17; calculation B12; calculation B13; calculation B30; calculation B31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service is manageable but exposed to rates. Net interest expense for the last twelve months was USD 80.5 million, covered 5.03x by reported EBITDA, and about 66.37% of principal floats; after the USD 100 million swap, a rise of 100 bp would add roughly USD 8.1 million a year, an analyst estimate. The financial covenants protect only the revolver and term loan A, 28.27% of principal, and the covenant definitions were not supplied, so headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15, 18, 21; calculation B10; calculation B11; calculation B26; calculation B27; calculation B29; calculation B33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main lever and it has leaned toward shareholders since the acquisition, which keeps the governance view at Medium. The Board raised the dividend and added USD 200 million to the repurchase authorization while net debt had not fallen, yet the record after the 2023 Kimball International acquisition, when debt was repaid, and the share-funded part of the Steelcase price argue for discipline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 37, 42–43; calculation B68; calculation B59; calculation B57

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a demand slowdown before synergies and debt reduction are delivered. An illustrative fall of 10% in last-twelve-months net sales would remove USD 218.9 million of gross profit at the 41.29% gross margin if costs did not respond, taking reported leverage to 6.70x, and still reach 4.21x if half the loss were offset by cost action, against covenant levels of 4.25x stepping to 3.50x on definitions that were not supplied. Management has levers, namely the dividend, repurchases, capital expenditure and restructuring, but each competes with the others for the same cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 35–37; calculation B34; calculation B35; calculation B36; calculation B37; calculation B39; calculation B41; calculation B48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that reported leverage on EBITDA before one-offs is 2.13x, that the third-quarter margin has returned to the prior-year level, that the equity is 58.07% of book capitalization and that no debt matures in size before 2029. Against that, goodwill and intangible assets are 36.08% of total assets and leave tangible equity of only USD 76.7 million, the added-back items recur in part, with restructuring and impairment charges of USD 51.9 million in the last twelve months, and the Q3 margin includes tariff refunds of unstated size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 30–34; calculation B8; calculation B19; calculation B20; calculation B43; calculation B44; calculation B45; calculation B54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if net debt fell below the year-end level of USD 1,083.9 million while last-twelve-months EBITDA held above USD 404.7 million, if free cash flow after dividends rose well above USD 39.5 million and if the 2029 notes were refinanced early. It would weaken if net sales fell year on year in the legacy business for two quarters, if the quarterly EBITDA margin dropped below the prior-year quarter, if repurchases were funded with revolver borrowings above the USD 169.0 million seasonal peak, or if the executed credit documents showed covenant headroom thinner than the house measures suggest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-04-04_hni-20260404.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation B2; calculation B16; calculation B9; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, market price, peer set or lender presentation was supplied, so the comparison with typical leveraged issuers in the sector and any market-implied view are not established, and the Average overall reading rests on absolute measures of scale, margin, cash flow and liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement's Consolidated EBITDA and covenant calculations were not supplied, so the stress case compares house leverage with covenant levels only directionally and neither a breach nor comfortable headroom can be concluded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Steelcase results before 2025-12-10 and any pro forma EBITDA were not supplied, so last-twelve-months EBITDA mixes perimeters and true run-rate leverage may be better or worse than 3.07x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The size of third-quarter tariff refunds is not stated, so how much of the margin recovery will repeat is not established and the second-quarter estimate stays an analyst inference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No backlog amount, order intake or book-to-bill was stated, and the annual report says backlog is cancellable and shipped within a few months, so revenue durability beyond the current quarter rests on channel mix and management comment and could change if order data showed a different trend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: HNI makes workplace furnishings, sold mainly through independent and company-owned dealers and office product distributors, and hearth products, sold through dealers, distributors and company-owned outlets; the company describes itself as the market leader in workplace furnishings and the leading hearth maker in North America, which is management language. After the Steelcase acquisition on 2025-12-10, Workplace Furnishings was 88.99% of nine-month net sales and Residential Building Products 11.01%, so cash flow now depends mostly on office spending, which is discretionary and project-based, while hearth earns 31.19% of segment operating income on housing and remodel demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 3–9, 16, 85; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 30; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B55; calculation B56; calculation B22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors the mix means cash flow visibility is moderate: sales are project-based and dealer-led, the filings give no backlog amount and say backlog is typically cancellable and fulfilled within a few months, and the integration of Steelcase through 2026 and the planned network optimization to 2028 will absorb cash before they add to it. The facilities are concentrated, with some production sites, people and key management located in a small area of eastern Iowa near the Mississippi River and several single-site plants, which makes a flood or storm a risk to production and cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: HNI is a listed company with no identified sponsor or controlling holder, one executive holds the Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer roles with a named Lead Director, and Business & governance rated governance and financial-policy risk Medium. Debt sits at the parent with certain domestic subsidiaries as guarantors, while USD 99.0 million of Steelcase notes remain unsecured obligations of a subsidiary and USD 351.0 million were exchanged into HNI senior secured notes, so the two groups of holders have different claims and ranking against the bank debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 106; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation B58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial policy evidence is mixed: acquisitions were repeated, the dividend and repurchase authorization were widened while net debt was higher than at year-end, but the 2024 repayment of USD 100 million of acquisition debt and the 55.03% share funding of the Steelcase price point to a tolerance for leverage that the Board has so far corrected after deals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2024-12-28_hni-20241228.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78; 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 106; calculation B9; calculation B59; calculation B57

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and partly discretionary. Workplace furnishings sells through a contract channel of large, customised, lengthy projects and a small and medium-sized business channel driven by price and delivery, and hybrid working has left office occupancy below historic levels, which the company says has and could continue to reduce demand. Legacy volume in Workplace Furnishings was lower in the first half of 2026, when the company cited soft volume and geopolitical uncertainty, and legacy Workplace Furnishings net sales rose 5.86% in the third quarter, so the trend has turned but is one quarter old.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is limited rather than absent: competitors offer similar products, price competition from lower-cost entrants constrains increases, and large customers and dealer consolidation add bargaining power, yet favourable price-cost was cited in the first and third quarters of 2026. In hearth, remodel-retrofit sales rose while new-home sales fell, so a housing slowdown would cut the higher-margin segment's volumes first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defensible in the legacy business but not yet in the combined one. The last-twelve-months gross margin of 41.29% and selling and administrative expenses of 33.50% of third-quarter net sales leave little room if volume falls, and Workplace Furnishings operating margin was 9.29% in Q3 2026 against 12.09% a year earlier after USD 24.8 million of purchase accounting amortization and USD 10.0 million of restructuring. Management levers are lean manufacturing, the Mexico plant, network optimization to 2028, Steelcase synergies focused on the Americas, and variable compensation, which rose in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 9, 45; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 30–34; calculation B49; calculation B50; calculation B52; calculation B67; calculation B35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings give no split of fixed and variable cost, so operating leverage is bounded only by the gross margin: a lost dollar of sales removes at most about 41 cents of gross profit before any cost response, which is the basis of the downside case below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate and partly discretionary. Capital expenditure including capitalized software was USD 91.1 million in nine months 2026 against USD 50.8 million a year earlier and USD 125 million to USD 130 million is expected for FY2026, which is above the USD 108.0 million of the last twelve months, while restructuring cash payments of USD 33.4 million, higher receivables and the settlement of acquisition accruals held nine-month operating cash flow to USD 163.3 million against USD 198.9 million a year earlier. Conversion of reported EBITDA to free cash flow was 32.79% over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 27, 35–36; calculation B14; calculation B46; calculation B47; calculation B61; calculation B60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Several claims sit outside total debt: lease obligations of USD 303.2 million, legacy Steelcase employee benefit obligations of USD 146.5 million and a HNI retiree medical subsidy of USD 15.3 million, purchase obligations of USD 154 million due in 2026 and USD 41 million after, letters of credit and surety bonds of about USD 58 million, trade letters of credit of USD 6 million, dealer guarantees of about USD 6 million, supplier finance of USD 31.2 million and customer deposits of USD 117.6 million, none of which are in the leverage ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 51, 120–121; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 23–24, 26; calculation B45; calculation B62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and is the force that matters most to margins: large competitors named in the annual report sell similar products and compete on price, delivery and service, and installed bases give them repeat orders, so share loss or price concessions would hit gross margin directly. Buyer power is moderate because the five largest customers are about 13% of sales, but dealer consolidation and dealer insolvency, which the company says can cause credit losses, add working capital risk. Supplier power is limited by multiple sources of steel, aluminium, lumber and textiles, while tariffs and freight cost raise input costs; substitutes include remote work and, as the company notes, uncertain effects of artificial intelligence on work patterns and specification.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These factors are material here. Office demand tracks employment, corporate profits and occupancy; hearth demand tracks housing starts, rates and affordability; the 2026 Supreme Court ruling against the emergency tariffs opened refunds that lifted second-quarter margins but make trade policy a source of volatile earnings; and the company states inflation, geopolitical uncertainty and housing softness shaped the third quarter. Each acts through lower volume or lower margin on a cost base that is larger after Steelcase, which is why they sit inside the downside case.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are scale, low customer concentration, a high-margin hearth business, positive free cash flow through the cycle and liquidity of USD 490.3 million. Weaknesses are elevated leverage, thin free cash flow after dividends, a margin still reset by purchase accounting and a heavy intangible balance. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are delivered Steelcase synergies, lower interest cost after the term loan B repricing and normalising capital expenditure. Threats are a demand slowdown before deleveraging, rate and tariff volatility, covenant step-downs and a refinancing of the 2029 notes into a weaker market.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B12; calculation B16; calculation B43

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is a strength because last-twelve-months net sales of USD 5,301.3 million and leading positions in two categories absorb shocks, and competitive advantage is average because brands and dealer networks help but patents are not material and price competition is steady. Business diversification is average: two segments but 88.99% in one, and low customer concentration offsets that. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with real levers but a larger asset base and unquantified fixed costs. Margin stability is weak for now at a 7.63% EBITDA margin against 12.44% in FY2024, free cash flow stability is average at USD 132.7 million with USD 39.5 million after dividends, and the ability to refinance is average because no maturity above USD 22.5 million falls before 2029 but the 2029 notes and springing maturities need action.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 6–9, 17–18; calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B14; calculation B16; calculation B55; calculation B32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is average to strong in level, at USD 490.3 million or 0.36x total debt, but seasonal, with a low of USD 327.4 million in April, and undrawn capacity may be overstated if letters of credit reduce the revolver. Financial policy and governance is average, consistent with the Medium governance risk level. Taken together the profile is average with a deteriorating-then-recovering trend; the missing datapoints are covenant definitions, order data, pro forma EBITDA and ratings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation B12; calculation B13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are Steelcase synergies that management calls slightly ahead of expectations, favourable price-cost, network optimization savings through 2028, the lower term loan B rate, and a Q3 margin already at the prior-year level. The headwinds are soft legacy volumes in the first half of 2026, housing affordability, geopolitical uncertainty, tariff refunds that will not repeat, net interest of USD 63.8 million in nine months 2026 against USD 18.9 million a year earlier and covenant step-downs. Over three to five years, management expects synergies to add to earnings over five years, while the 2029 notes, 2030 facilities and 2032 term loan must be refinanced and demand for offices remains uncertain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 51; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 30, 35; calculation B19; calculation B20; calculation B10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a slowdown in corporate office orders, hearth demand from housing, or both, on top of tariff and input-cost shocks. The first operational break is volume: with a gross margin of 41.29% and no stated fixed-cost split, a 10% fall in last-twelve-months net sales of USD 530.1 million would remove USD 218.9 million of gross profit if costs did not respond, cutting reported EBITDA to USD 185.8 million, lifting net debt over EBITDA to 6.70x and reducing EBITDA over net interest to 2.31x. If management offset half the loss through cost actions, EBITDA would be USD 295.2 million, leverage 4.21x and interest cover 3.67x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B34; calculation B35; calculation B36; calculation B37; calculation B38; calculation B39; calculation B40; calculation B41; calculation B42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission then runs through cash: free cash flow after dividends of USD 39.5 million would turn negative, the revolver would be drawn from USD 380.0 million of undrawn capacity, and floating-rate interest on about 66.37% of principal would add to the burden if rates rose. The covenant maximum falls toward 3.50x on credit agreement definitions that were not supplied, so a covenant conversation would be the observable trigger, with dividend and repurchase cuts, capital expenditure of USD 125 million to USD 130 million and restructuring as the levers. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis in the half-offset case because liquidity of USD 490.3 million is large against scheduled principal, but protection of the 4.25x to 3.50x covenant path cannot be shown without action, because the covenant definitions were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18, 21, 36; calculation B12; calculation B16; calculation B26; calculation B27; calculation B61; calculation B48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Hni Corp presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, low customer concentration, a high-margin hearth segment and consistent free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that has not fallen in absolute terms, thin free cash flow after dividends and earnings still reset by Steelcase. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow was positive in FY2024, FY2025 and the last twelve months, though it is seasonal and thin after dividends. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivering EBITDA growth and net debt reduction before 2028, when the 2029 notes and springing maturities come into view. The primary downside path is a demand slowdown before synergies and paydown arrive. Further analysis would require the credit documents, a company EBITDA bridge, ratings, market prices and a peer set; a comparison with typical leveraged issuers in the sector is not established. Top risk: leverage staying near the covenant path while demand softens.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B5; calculation B14; calculation B16; calculation B48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is scale with low concentration: last-twelve-months net sales of USD 5,301.3 million and five largest customers of about 13% of sales spread revenue across many dealers and projects, so no customer loss alone threatens debt service. The second is cash generation: free cash flow was USD 173.8 million in FY2024, USD 208.5 million in FY2025 and USD 132.7 million over the last twelve months, which covers interest and scheduled amortization. The third is the hearth segment, earning a 17.81% margin and 31.19% of segment operating income, which cushions the larger furniture segment while housing holds. The fourth is liquidity and maturities, with USD 490.3 million of cash and undrawn revolver and no more than USD 22.5 million of scheduled principal a year until 2029. The fifth is the cost and synergy programme, which management says is slightly ahead of expectations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_hni-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-10-03_hni-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 30; calculation B12; calculation B14; calculation B66; calculation B21; calculation B22; calculation B32; calculation B1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is leverage that has not fallen in absolute terms, with net debt of USD 1,244.2 million, USD 160.3 million above year-end, which leaves less cushion against the covenant ladder. The second is thin free cash flow after dividends, USD 39.5 million over the last twelve months, which slows repayment. The third is earnings quality: a 7.63% EBITDA margin, provisional purchase accounting, restructuring that recurs and refunds of unstated size. The fourth is cyclical, housing-linked demand with limited visibility, and the fifth is a 2029 note maturity of USD 450.0 million with springing maturities in the facilities, which brings a refinancing test forward.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B5; calculation B9; calculation B3; calculation B16; calculation B30
